name: Cochin Shipyard Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest public-sector shipbuilder and ship-repair yard (government 63.3% after Sep 2026 change), building commercial vessels (offshore, cruise/ferry, tankers, wind-farm vessels) and defence ships (IAC-1 carrier built; ASW-SWC, NGMV). FY26 consolidated sales Rs5,022 cr (-1%), TTM Rs5,047 cr, EBITDA Rs763 cr (15%), other income Rs423 cr, PAT Rs680 cr. Order book about Rs21,900 cr (Sahi, 2026-09-10); FY27 EBITDA margin guide ~14%. Q1 FY27 sales Rs1,094 cr, PAT Rs151 cr. Market cap Rs32,605 cr at 48x P/E; borrowings Rs1,672 cr for the Rs6,000 cr expansion.

exposures.mechanism: Shipbuilding financial assistance, ISRF (Cochin seeks shareholder nod for Rs1,800 cr ISRF transfer, 2026-10-07) and Maritime India infrastructure support underpin a Rs6,000 cr Vallarpadam/Thoothukudi project plan (2026-10-09). +1 SSU (stronger support) => capacity/orders ~+10% over 3 years; EBITDA +12%; EV/MCap ~1.0; persistence 0.7 => ~+4.

evidence.note: Business Standard: plans Rs6,000 cr projects in Vallarpadam and Thoothukudi; scanx: ISRF Rs1,800 cr transfer

exposures.mechanism: Naval/defence vessels (IAC-2 follow-on, ASW-SWC, NGMV, auxiliaries) give a large share of the order book (model knowledge, ~40%+). +10% domestic defence orders => ~+4% order inflow => EBITDA +5%, persistence 0.6 => ~+3.

Freight/charter strength lifts newbuild ordering and repair/refit demand; commercial orders (40 ships from US and other countries, 2026-10-09; European cruise/ferry vessels) are the growth leg. +25% rates => ~+5% order flow, x1.3 op. leverage x0.5 => +2.0.

Steel plate/sections ~12% of contract cost; escalation clauses cover part. +7% => 0.84% of sales vs 15% margin = -5.6% EBITDA; ~50% unrecovered => -2.8% x persistence 0.5 => -1.4, rounded to -1.5. FY27 EBITDA margin guided to ~14% vs 15% TTM (Business Standard 2026-09-11).

International contracts (Europe, US owners) billed in USD/EUR are ~25-30% of order book (model knowledge); imports (engines, equipment) are hedged. +3% USD/INR => +0.4% margin => +1.5% EBITDA, x0.5 persistence => ~+1.0.

Borrowings rose to Rs1,672 cr (Mar 2026) for capex; interest Rs111 cr TTM; treasury income Rs423 cr offsets: net +25bp ~ flat for earnings; discount-rate effect on 48x P/E negative. Repo 5.50% since 2026-10-07.

evidence.note: Google News: Reuters 2026-10-07 'India first hike in nearly 4 years'; SCC Online 'repo to 5.50%, calibrated tightening'

exposures.mechanism: Disruption raises freight rates and newbuild demand, but war risk also delays deliveries/insurance; ambiguous, +0.8.
Offshore support vessels, tankers and ONGC/oil-linked repair; empirical +1.37 per +10% (t=1.3) mostly beta 2.1. Fundamental effect small positive.

Beta ~2.0-2.2, 1y vol 39%, stock -30% in 12m and -17% in 3m after FY27 margin guidance disappointment (2026-09-11: -9% to -12% over two sessions) and a lower promoter holding (67.91% to 63.33% in Sep 2026 quarter, consistent with a block/OFS; not verified).
US-based owners and parts; tariffs could raise vessel cost/competitiveness issues; offset if US-China port-fee measures push owners to Indian yards. Ambiguous; low confidence.
